answer: Juries get redrawn at random every round. A faker can't predict who grades them next, so they can't bribe or plant enough fake judges. One lucky round buys nothing. To win, they'd have to fool a fresh crowd every time. That's like keeping a garden green through a gale. The effort piles up and the payoff shrinks. Honest agents just show up and do the work. They find an oasis of trust without ever knowing the jury.
